name: Law of Conservation of Mass
subject: chemistry
ncert_reference: NCERT textbook portal; Class 9 atoms and molecules activity page to verify
educational_goal: Compare total mass before and after a chemical reaction in a closed system.
safety_notes: Use small quantities and eye protection.
Do not seal a rigid container during gas production.

scenes.description: A conical flask with vinegar supports a balloon containing baking soda, positioned on a digital balance before and after mixing.
scenes.image_url: PLACEHOLDER: add a license-reviewed closed-reaction photo

steps.description: Place baking soda in a balloon and vinegar in a flask without mixing them.
steps.observation: Reactants are separated while the complete apparatus can be weighed.
steps.key_visual: Reactants are separated while the complete apparatus can be weighed.

scenes.description: A conical flask with vinegar supports a balloon containing baking soda, positioned on a digital balance before and after mixing.

steps.description: Attach the balloon to the flask and measure the mass of the closed arrangement.
steps.observation: The initial total mass is recorded.
steps.key_visual: The initial total mass is recorded.

steps.description: Lift the balloon so the baking soda falls into the vinegar.
steps.observation: Fizzing occurs and the balloon inflates as gas forms.
steps.key_visual: Fizzing occurs and the balloon inflates as gas forms.

scenes.description: A conical flask with vinegar supports a balloon containing baking soda, positioned on a digital balance before and after mixing.

steps.description: Measure the mass again without opening the arrangement.
steps.observation: The total mass remains approximately unchanged in the closed system.
steps.key_visual: The total mass remains approximately unchanged in the closed system.
